name: Annapurna
tagline: Teahouse trails from Gurung villages to Thorong La
meta_description: Annapurna treks and tours: Poon Hill, Annapurna Base Camp, the Circuit over Thorong La, Mardi Himal, Khopra and ABC heli tours. Prices, seasons and permits.
summary: The Annapurna region, north of Pokhara, is Nepal's most varied trekking area: 3-day village walks to Ghandruk, 4-day Poon Hill loops, 11-day treks to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130 m and the 15-day Circuit over Thorong La at 5,416 m. Best months are October–November and March–April; an ACAP permit is required.
intro: The Annapurna massif rises less than 40 km north of Pokhara, and the hills between the lake and the snow hold the densest network of teahouse trails in Nepal. Annapurna I, at 8,091 m, was the first 8,000 m peak ever climbed, in 1950, but most visitors come for what lies below it: Gurung and Magar villages of stone and slate, rhododendron forests that flower red in spring, and viewpoints such as Poon Hill and Khopra Danda that face Dhaulagiri across the Kali Gandaki gorge.

The region suits almost every kind of traveller. Families with young children can drive to Ghandruk in 3 hours and walk out over two gentle days. First-time trekkers can reach Poon Hill at 3,210 m in four days from Pokhara. Fitter walkers head up the Modi Khola gorge to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130 m, ringed by peaks above 7,000 m, or along the ridge to Mardi Himal Base Camp below Machhapuchhre. For those who cannot walk, a helicopter reaches ABC from Pokhara in 25–30 minutes.

On the north side of the range, the Annapurna Circuit follows the Marsyangdi valley to Manang at 3,519 m, a Tibetan Buddhist village in the rain shadow, and crosses Thorong La at 5,416 m to the temple town of Muktinath. Roads now reach both Manang and Muktinath, so we drive the lower sections and walk the high ones. Side trips lead to Tilicho Lake at 4,919 m, and climbers can tackle Pisang Peak, 6,091 m, with an NMA permit.

Everything here runs on teahouses: family lodges with twin rooms, shared or attached bathrooms and dining rooms heated by a stove, serving dal bhat with free refills. The whole region lies inside the Annapurna Conservation Area, the first and largest of Nepal's conservation areas, so every trekker needs an ACAP permit. Our packages include permits, licensed guides, porters, transport and meals, with prices in both INR and USD.

highlights.title: Poon Hill sunrise
highlights.text: From the tower on Poon Hill, 3,210 m, more than twenty peaks line the horizon at dawn, from Dhaulagiri at 8,167 m to Machhapuchhre. It is reached in four days from Pokhara with a top sleeping altitude of 2,874 m in Ghorepani, which makes it the most popular first trek in Nepal.

highlights.title: Inside the Annapurna Sanctuary
highlights.text: Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130 m sits in a natural amphitheatre enclosed by Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna and Machhapuchhre. The only way in on foot is the narrow Modi Khola gorge, a 4-day walk up from the road through Chhomrong and Deurali, or 25–30 minutes by helicopter.

highlights.title: Thorong La and the Circuit
highlights.text: The Annapurna Circuit crosses Thorong La at 5,416 m, one of the highest trekking passes in the world, after two acclimatisation nights in Manang. The descent of about 1,700 m leads to Muktinath, sacred to Hindus and Buddhists, and the dry Kali Gandaki valley on the edge of Mustang.

highlights.title: Gurung villages and Gurkha history
highlights.text: Ghandruk, Landruk and Chhomrong are Gurung villages of slate roofs and stone lanes, home to families with long traditions of service in the Gurkha regiments. Ghandruk's museum, the Tamu Lhosar new year celebrations around 30 December and homestay dinners show a living culture on the trail.

highlights.title: Quieter ridges: Mardi Himal and Khopra
highlights.text: Mardi Himal's ridge trail climbs to about 4,500 m below Machhapuchhre's south face in a week from Pokhara, while Khopra Danda's community lodge at 3,660 m faces Dhaulagiri across the Kali Gandaki. Both see a fraction of the trekkers on the ABC trail and suit people who want space.

highlights.title: Tilicho Lake and Pisang Peak
highlights.text: Above Manang, Tilicho Lake fills a basin at 4,919 m below the ice of Tilicho Peak, a 2–3 day side trip with a dramatic scree traverse. Nearby, Pisang Peak at 6,091 m offers a first Himalayan summit for climbers with crampon skills, using an NMA climbing permit and a licensed climbing guide.

getting_there: Pokhara is the gateway to almost every Annapurna trek. From Kathmandu it is a 25-minute flight or a 200 km drive of 6–8 hours on the Prithvi Highway; tourist buses leave Kathmandu each morning. From Pokhara, jeeps reach the main trailheads in 45 minutes to 3 hours: Kande for Mardi Himal and the Australian Camp trail, Hile and Ulleri for Poon Hill, Ghandruk and Kimche for the village treks, and Siwai for Annapurna Base Camp. The Annapurna Circuit starts at Besisahar, 6–7 hours by road from Kathmandu or 4 hours from Pokhara, with jeeps onward to Chame and Manang. Most Circuit trekkers finish at Jomsom and fly back to Pokhara in about 20 minutes, weather permitting. Travellers from India can fly to Kathmandu or cross by road at Sunauli–Bhairahawa, about 8 hours from Pokhara.
permits: Every trekker in the region needs an Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) permit: NPR 3,000 for foreign nationals and NPR 1,000 for SAARC nationals, including Indians; children under 10 have generally been exempt. Permits are issued at Nepal Tourism Board offices in Kathmandu and Pokhara and checked at points along the main trails. Since 1 April 2023 Nepal's rules require foreign trekkers in conservation areas to walk with a licensed guide booked through a registered agency; enforcement on Annapurna trails has varied, and the TIMS card rule has changed more than once. Climbing Pisang Peak or Chulu needs an NMA permit. Check current status before you travel.

months.weather: Ghorepani −6 to 8 °C, Pokhara 7 to 20 °C, dry with clear mornings
months.summary: January is cold and quiet, with some of the clearest air of the year. Lower treks such as Ghandruk, Poon Hill and the luxury lodge route are very good: sunny days, frosty dawns and empty trails. Snow can fall above 3,000 m, so Annapurna Base Camp needs care above Deurali, and Thorong La is often closed after storms. Lodges stay open on the popular lower routes, while some at High Camp and Tilicho Base Camp close for winter.
months.tip: Pack a sleeping bag rated to −10 °C even for Poon Hill, because lodge rooms are unheated.

months.weather: Ghorepani −4 to 10 °C, Pokhara 9 to 23 °C, mostly dry, late-month storms
months.summary: February warms slowly but still brings cold nights and the chance of heavy snow higher up. The Poon Hill and Ghandruk loops remain the best choices, with clear views and few trekkers. Annapurna Base Camp is possible but avalanche risk between Deurali and Machhapuchhre Base Camp rises after big snowfalls, so follow ACAP advice. Thorong La is usually still snowbound. By late February the first rhododendrons start flowering at lower elevations.
months.tip: Ask your guide about avalanche warnings above Deurali before committing to Annapurna Base Camp in February.

months.weather: Ghorepani 0 to 14 °C, ABC −8 to 6 °C, warming, afternoon haze
months.summary: March opens the spring season. Rhododendrons bloom across the forests between Ghorepani, Tadapani and the Mardi Himal ridge, peaking from late March into April. Mornings are usually clear, with haze and cloud building in the afternoon. Annapurna Base Camp and Mardi Himal are busy again, and Thorong La opens as snow consolidates, though early-March crossings can still be blocked. Watch for avalanche-prone sections above Deurali after late snowfalls.
months.tip: Start walking by 7 am in March to see the peaks before the afternoon haze.

months.weather: Ghorepani 4 to 17 °C, Manang −3 to 15 °C, warm days, occasional storms
months.summary: April is the best spring month on most trails. The rhododendron forests around Ghorepani, Poon Hill and Khopra are in full colour, temperatures are comfortable and Thorong La is usually open. Views are best early in the day, with clouds and occasional thunderstorms later. It is a good time for the Annapurna Circuit, Khopra Danda and Pisang Peak. Tilicho Lake is still largely frozen. Lodges are busy but less crowded than in October.
months.tip: Book Ghorepani and Thorong Phedi lodges ahead for April, when spring trekking peaks.

months.weather: Pokhara 20 to 30 °C, Manang 0 to 17 °C, hazy, pre-monsoon showers
months.summary: May is warm and increasingly hazy, with pre-monsoon cloud and showers building through the month. High routes remain good: Manang, Thorong La and Tilicho are at their warmest, and Tilicho Lake starts to thaw. Lower trails become hot and humid below 2,000 m, and mountain views from Poon Hill are less reliable. It is a reasonable month for the Circuit and Pisang Peak, less so for photography of distant peaks.
months.tip: Carry a light rain jacket every day in May, as afternoon showers become common.

months.weather: Pokhara 22 to 30 °C, heavy rain from mid-June, Manang drier
months.summary: The monsoon usually arrives in mid-June. Pokhara and the southern slopes receive heavy rain, leeches appear on forest trails and landslides begin to affect roads to Siwai, Ghandruk and Besisahar. Cloud hides most views. Upper Manang lies in the rain shadow and stays much drier, so the upper Circuit is possible with flexible plans, but the jeep road up the Marsyangdi is often blocked. We do not sell most Annapurna treks this month.
months.tip: If you must trek in June, choose the upper Manang valley and allow two spare days for road delays.

months.weather: Pokhara 23 to 30 °C, wettest month, Manang light rain
months.summary: July is the wettest month on the southern side of the Annapurnas, with Pokhara receiving some of the heaviest rainfall in Nepal. Trails are muddy and leech-infested, rivers run high and landslides frequently close roads. Mountain views are rare. The rain-shadow valley around Manang gets far less rain and stays green and quiet, but reaching it is unreliable. Flights to Jomsom are often cancelled by cloud.
months.tip: Travel insurance with trip interruption cover is essential for monsoon travel in Nepal.

months.weather: Pokhara 23 to 30 °C, heavy rain continues, clearer spells late
months.summary: August remains wet, with heavy rain, leeches and landslides on the southern trails. Hindu pilgrims walk to Khayer Lake above Khopra around Janai Purnima, usually in August, but conditions are hard. Manang and the upper Circuit are drier but access is slow. Late August sometimes brings longer clear spells, and botanists enjoy the wildflowers in the high pastures. Most trekkers wait for September.
months.tip: Wear long socks over trousers and carry salt or repellent for leeches on monsoon trails.

months.weather: Ghorepani 10 to 19 °C, Pokhara 21 to 29 °C, rain easing, clearer late
months.summary: The monsoon usually eases during September, with mornings becoming clearer towards the end of the month. Trails are lush and green, rice terraces turn gold, and lodges reopen fully. Early September can still bring heavy showers and landslides, so road access to Siwai and Besisahar should be checked. By late September, Annapurna Base Camp, Poon Hill and the Circuit are good, with fewer crowds than in October.
months.tip: Book late-September departures for green terraces and quieter trails before the October peak.

months.weather: Ghorepani 6 to 17 °C, ABC −4 to 10 °C, Manang −5 to 14 °C, clear and dry
months.summary: October is the best month in the Annapurna region and the busiest. Skies are clear, temperatures are comfortable and every trail is open, from Poon Hill to Thorong La and Tilicho. Dashain, Nepal's biggest festival, usually falls in late September or October, and Tihar follows in October or November, so buses and flights fill with Nepalis travelling home. Book lodges and flights early, and expect company at Poon Hill and Annapurna Base Camp.
months.tip: Reserve Jomsom and Pokhara flights early in October, when festival travel fills seats.

months.weather: Ghorepani 2 to 14 °C, ABC −8 to 7 °C, Manang −9 to 12 °C, very clear
months.summary: November is often the clearest month of the year, with crisp air and stable weather. Days are pleasant and nights cold, especially above 3,500 m. It is excellent for photography on Poon Hill, Khopra Danda and Mardi Himal, and for crossing Thorong La before winter snow arrives. Trails are slightly quieter than in October. Tilicho Lake begins to freeze at the edges late in the month.
months.tip: Bring warm gloves and a down jacket in November, as dawn temperatures drop well below freezing above 3,000 m.

months.weather: Ghorepani −4 to 10 °C, Pokhara 8 to 21 °C, dry, clear, cold nights
months.summary: December brings cold, clear and quiet conditions. The lower treks are lovely, with sharp views and few crowds, and the Gurung villages celebrate Tamu Lhosar, the Gurung new year, around 30 December. Annapurna Base Camp is possible with warm gear. Thorong La can close after the first heavy snowfalls, so Circuit plans need flexibility from mid-December, and Tilicho Lake is frozen.
months.tip: Time a Ghandruk trek to end on 30 December to see Tamu Lhosar celebrations in the village.

faqs.q: Which is the best trek in the Annapurna region?
faqs.a: It depends on your time and fitness. Poon Hill suits beginners and families in 4–5 days. Annapurna Base Camp is the best all-round trek of 10–12 days, reaching 4,130 m in the Sanctuary. The Annapurna Circuit is the classic long trek of 14–16 days over Thorong La. Mardi Himal and Khopra Danda are quieter week-long alternatives.

faqs.q: How much does an Annapurna trek cost?
faqs.a: Our packages start from about ₹19,000 or US$220 for a 3-day Ghandruk trek, ₹29,000 or US$340 for the 4-day Poon Hill loop, ₹78,000 or US$910 for 11-day ABC and ₹1,04,000 or US$1,210 for the 15-day Circuit, per person on twin sharing. Prices include guides, porters, permits, teahouses and trail meals.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Annapurna treks?
faqs.a: Yes. Every trekker needs an ACAP permit: NPR 3,000 for foreigners and NPR 1,000 for SAARC nationals including Indians. Since 2023, Nepal's rules require foreign trekkers in conservation areas to walk with a licensed guide, though enforcement on Annapurna has varied. Climbing peaks need NMA permits. Check current status before you travel; our packages include permits.

faqs.q: What is the best time to trek in Annapurna?
faqs.a: October and November give the clearest skies and most stable weather. March and April are the second season, with rhododendrons in bloom. December to February is good for lower treks but cold, with Thorong La often closed. June to September is monsoon, with rain, leeches and landslides on the southern side, though upper Manang stays drier.

faqs.q: Can beginners trek in the Annapurna region?
faqs.a: Yes. The Annapurna region has some of Nepal's best beginner treks. Ghandruk in 3 days and Poon Hill in 4–5 days stay below 3,300 m with daily walks of 3–6 hours. Beginners with good fitness can also do Annapurna Base Camp with training. The Circuit and Tilicho are better after previous trekking experience.

faqs.q: How do I get to the Annapurna region from India?
faqs.a: Fly to Kathmandu and connect to Pokhara by a 25-minute flight or a 6–8 hour drive. By road, cross at Sunauli–Bhairahawa and drive about 8 hours to Pokhara. Indian nationals need a passport or voter ID; no visa is required. From Pokhara, jeeps reach the trailheads in 45 minutes to 3 hours.

faqs.q: Is there a helicopter tour to Annapurna Base Camp?
faqs.a: Yes. Helicopter tours from Pokhara fly to Annapurna Base Camp in 25–30 minutes, land for about 15–20 minutes and return, taking about 2 hours in total. Shared seats start from about US$650 per person. Flights run only in clear morning weather, and people with heart or lung conditions or pregnant women should not fly.

faqs.q: Will I get altitude sickness on Annapurna treks?
faqs.a: Low treks like Ghandruk and Poon Hill rarely cause problems. Above about 3,500 m, on ABC, Mardi Himal, the Circuit and Tilicho, mild symptoms are common and serious altitude sickness is possible. Ascend gradually, take acclimatisation days in Manang, drink plenty, avoid alcohol and descend if symptoms worsen. Insurance with helicopter evacuation is essential.

faqs.q: What are teahouses like on Annapurna trails?
faqs.a: Teahouses are family-run lodges with twin rooms, shared or attached bathrooms and a dining room heated by a stove. Menus offer dal bhat with free refills, noodles, pasta, potatoes and breakfasts. Rooms cost NPR 500–1,000 or less if you eat there, and prices rise with altitude. Bring a warm sleeping bag for higher nights.
